newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Leading Kuwaiti MP survives assassination bid.
newsitem.headline: Leading Kuwaiti MP survives assassination bid.

text.p: A leading Kuwaiti opposition parliamentarian was shot twice in an assassination attempt on Friday and parliamentary sources said he was in stable condition.

Pro-democracy veteran Abdullah al-Naibari, 61, was rushed to a hospital south of Kuwait City with bullet wounds in his jaw and shoulder along with his wife Feryal al-Furaih who was injured in the shoulder, an Interior Ministry spokesman said.
"I think he will make it. I do not think that he is in a life-threatening situation," a political source said.
Parliamentarians who went to Adan Hospital said Naibari's shoulder wound was superficial and that doctors will operate on his jaw. His wife's wound was also superficial, they said.

Naibari, a leading government critic who has also opposed some Islamist bills in parliament, was driving home in Kuwait City from his beachhouse close to the southern border with Saudi Arabia when shot.
An Interior Ministry spokesman denounced the attack and vowed swift action to arrest the attackers. Police sources said two vehicles were involved in the attempt.
Acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah said the attack was meant to trigger a "strife".
The attack was not directed against "a person or a group of persons, it was (directed) against the Kuwaiti people and Kuwait."
Parliament Speaker Ahmad al-Saadoun told journalists at the hospital where Naibari received treatment that "corrupt elements" were behind the attack.
"The matters of the state were left in the hands of corrupt elements," said Saadoun, adding that Naibari was shot because of his campaign against "public funds thieves."

Leading Shi'ite Moslem parliamentary deputy Adnan Abdul-Samad condemned the shooting and said "elements in the country whose interests were damaged by parliament and by democracy were behind such attacks."
In a similar incident, former MP Hamad al-Jouan was crippled in an assassination attempt in 1991 weeks after Kuwait's liberation from a seven-month Iraqi occupation.
Jouan and Naibari were members of parliament when it was dissolved in 1986. Both were the most prominent campaigners for the restoration of democracy that was achieved in 1992.
